course.programmeTitle: Bachelor of Engineering in Data Science and Engineering
course.title: Ethics and Responsible Data Science
course.prerequisites: IDS101 Introduction to Data Science and Engineering APR102 Advanced Programming (Intro. to Python and OOP) STA102 Statistics I: Statistics for Engineers PAN202 Predictive Analytics (with Python) DMM302 Data Mining and Machine Learning
course.description: This course aims to establish the ethical foundations essential for professional practice in computing, providing students with a comprehensive understanding of key ethical issues and professional responsibilities related to the development and utilisation of computers and information systems. This study will present a foundational overview of ethical theories and examine the function of professional organisations in upholding best practices, first in a general context and subsequently within the computing industry. The discussion will encompass legislation relevant to the computing industry, focussing on three primary ethical concerns: computer hacking, data privacy, and intellectual property. This course will also present ethical principles and practices in data science aimed at addressing public and corporate concerns regarding bias and other unintended harmful effects arising from data science models. The course provides a structured framework for implementing data science projects, along with a systematic audit process for their evaluation.

clos.description: Analyse the fundamental concepts of ethics, morality, law, and professional standards within the computing industry.
Evaluate the characteristics of intellectual property, privacy, anonymity, and computer crimes, along with their consequences for individuals, organisations, communities, and societies.

Evaluate the potential unintended harm that may emerge and the impact of predictors in black box models through interpretability methods, alongside assessing model performance using metrics to quantify bias and unfairness.
Implement a Responsible Data Science framework in sample projects.
Perform an ethical audit of a data science project to identify potential harms and areas for bias mitigation or harm reduction.

topics.title: Topic 1: Introduction to Responsible Data Science
topics.llosRaw: Explain the historical context and motivation for responsible data science Define Responsible Data Science (RDS) and articulate the three core themes Differentiate between the ethical problems of bias and unfairness

topics.title: Topic 2: Modelling, Blackbox Algorithm, and Legal Implications
topics.llosRaw: Analyze predictive models and distinguish between intrinsically interpretable models and black-box models Evaluate model performance for classification tasks using metrics

topics.title: Topic 3: Responsible Data Science Framework
topics.llosRaw: Identify how AI systems can go wrong, recognizing the difference between intentional malicious uses and unintended consequences Summarize the key elements of the legal and regulatory landscape impacting AI

topics.title: Topic 4: Model Interpretability
topics.llosRaw: Analyze the primary motivations leading to the creation of harmful AI, and the resulting lack of consideration for the broader real-world context Describe the key principles underlying contemporary responsible data science frameworks Apply the stages of the Responsible Data Science (RDS) Framework Create the foundational documentation artifacts necessary for RDS

topics.title: Topic 5: Responsible Data Science Project and Audit
topics.llosRaw: Articulate why model interpretability is crucial for responsible data science Evaluate the trade-off between maximizing predictive performance and maintaining model interpretability Differentiate between local methods (explaining individual predictions) and global methods Utilize interpretability methods Establish a Four-Measure Performance Baseline to systematically benchmark model choices against one another

topics.title: Topic 6: Ethics for the Computing Professions
topics.llosRaw: Define the concept of professional ethics and differentiate it from legal responsibility Analyze the essential elements and objectives of a professional code of ethics Identify and describe the eight primary professional principles that software engineers must adhere to Describe the importance of accountability, continuous evaluation, and adherence to rules and guidelines within an organization

topics.title: Topic 7: Privacy and Anonymity
topics.llosRaw: Explain the ambiguous concept of privacy Analyze the economic impact of privacy violation Evaluate the ethicality of privacy violations

topics.title: Topic 8: Intellectual Property
topics.llosRaw: Trace the historical progression of intellectual property protection Identify major international efforts to protect intellectual property Classify and describe the main illegal methods used for software piracy Analyze the multifaceted economic and social factors that encourage software piracy

topics.title: Topic 9: Computer and Information Crimes
topics.llosRaw: Distinguish between the two dimensions of information security Characterize the major types of malicious software Analyze the three general categories that cause unethical or illegal behavior in information security

topics.title: Topic 10: Mini Project
topics.llosRaw: Identify the signs and harm caused by computer viruses Explain the concept and methods of hacking Formulate and implement prevention strategies to protect against computer crimes

topics.title: Topic 11: Recap on Responsible Data Science in Practice
topics.llosRaw: Apply the Responsible Data Science (RDS) Framework end-to-end to an ethically fraught modeling task Demonstrate advanced technical rigor by fitting and comparing multiple models and architectures Conduct a comprehensive audit of the final candidate model Synthesize the project findings and audit results to justify the final model choice and propose actionable policy recommendations

studentResponsibilitiesRaw: Read the learning materials beforehand which means to be ready for the next session. Be completely engaged in class, active, take notes, and ask questions in class. Students are required to participate in various activities in and out of the classroom, such as group work, and individual homework for assignments and reports assigned by the subject teacher. Submit the assigned tasks such as homework, assignments, or research proposal on time.
coursePolicyRaw: Attendance & Preparation Students are expected to attend all classes (online/on-site). Assigned readings and preparation outlines must be completed before class if any. Active participation in group discussions and post-chapter evaluations is required. Academic Integrity All assignments, quizzes, and exams must be done individually. Academic misconduct includes: - Presenting others’ work as one’s own. - Engaging in plagiarism or cheating. Homework & Assignments Preparation outlines must be submitted on time; late submissions incur penalties. Peer discussion is encouraged, but midterm and final exams must be independent. Examinations Midterm and final exams are closed-book. Penalties Violations of academic integrity may result in a failing grade and referral to the Office of Student Affairs. Students uncertain about potential violations should consult the instructor in advance.
